[package]
name = "bivvy"
version = "1.7.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.93"
description = "Interactive development environment setup automation"
license-file = "LICENSE"
repository = "https://github.com/bivvy-dev/bivvy"
keywords = ["cli", "setup", "development", "automation"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[dependencies]
# CLI framework
clap = { version = "4.5.56", features = ["derive", "env"] }

# Interactive prompts
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
console = "0.16.2"

# Progress indicators
indicatif = "0.18.3"

# Serialization
serde = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.149"

# YAML parsing
serde_yaml = "0.9"

# YAML with source location tracking (for lint error reporting)
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1.0.100"
thiserror = "2.0.18"

# File system
dirs = "6.0.0"
walkdir = "2.5.0"
glob = "0.3.3"

# Process execution
which = "8.0.0"

# HTTP client (for remote templates)
reqwest = { version = "0.13.1", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls"] }

# Time handling (for state)
chrono = { version = "0.4.43", features = ["serde"] }

# Hashing (for project identification)
sha2 = "0.10"
hex = "0.4.3"

# Random number generation (for session IDs)
getrandom = "0.2"

# Regular expressions (for version extraction)
regex = "1"

# Logging
tracing = "0.1.44"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3.22", features = ["env-filter"] }

# Embed templates at compile time
include_dir = "0.7.4"
clap_complete = "4.5.65"

# URL handling (for feedback delivery)
open = "5"
urlencoding = "2"

[dev-dependencies]
assert_cmd = "2.1.2"
httpmock = "0.8"
predicates = "3.1.3"
tempfile = "3.24.0"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

[profile.release]
lto = true
strip = true
codegen-units = 1
opt-level = "z"

content.text:
Done. Here's a summary of the fix:

**Root cause:** Pressing Ctrl+D during interactive prompts could cause a panic because:
1. The custom `prompt_yes_no` function didn't handle `Key::Char('\x04')` (Ctrl+D in raw mode) — it looped forever or propagated an unhelpful IO error
2. EOF errors from `dialoguer`/`console` were wrapped as generic `BivvyError::Io` with no clean exit path
3. The cursor was hidden but never restored on error paths in `prompt_yes_no`

**Changes across 3 files:**

- **`src/error.rs`** — Added `BivvyError::UserCancelled` variant and `is_user_cancelled()` helper method
- **`src/ui/prompts.rs`** — `map_dialoguer_err` now converts EOF errors to `UserCancelled`; added `map_io_eof` helper; `prompt_yes_no` explicitly catches `Key::Char('\x04')` and always restores the cursor (even on error) via extracted `prompt_yes_no_loop`
- **`src/main.rs`** — `UserCancelled` errors print "Cancelled." and exit with code 130 (standard for user interrupts) instead of showing an error message

**7 new tests** covering the `UserCancelled` variant, EOF-to-cancellation conversion, and IO passthrough behavior.

Done. Here's a summary of the fix:

**Root cause:** Pressing Ctrl+D during interactive prompts could cause a panic because:
1. The custom `prompt_yes_no` function didn't handle `Key::Char('\x04')` (Ctrl+D in raw mode) — it looped forever or propagated an unhelpful IO error
2. EOF errors from `dialoguer`/`console` were wrapped as generic `BivvyError::Io` with no clean exit path
3. The cursor was hidden but never restored on error paths in `prompt_yes_no`

**Changes across 3 files:**

- **`src/error.rs`** — Added `BivvyError::UserCancelled` variant and `is_user_cancelled()` helper method
- **`src/ui/prompts.rs`** — `map_dialoguer_err` now converts EOF errors to `UserCancelled`; added `map_io_eof` helper; `prompt_yes_no` explicitly catches `Key::Char('\x04')` and always restores the cursor (even on error) via extracted `prompt_yes_no_loop`
- **`src/main.rs`** — `UserCancelled` errors print "Cancelled." and exit with code 130 (standard for user interrupts) instead of showing an error message

**7 new tests** covering the `UserCancelled` variant, EOF-to-cancellation conversion, and IO passthrough behavior.
